solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Initially served up some hotpot, Irish dish

indicators.note: initially tells us to take the opening letter of each of the following five words

explanation.surface: A waiter dishes out some hotpot, a hearty Irish dish, to begin a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irish dish' looks like the definition, but Irish is the last word picked from, and 'dish' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese preparation of vinegared rice with raw fish, served as a dish.

clue.text: Son arrived after work and left in old plane

indicators.note: after places the word for arrived later in the sequence

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
with can mean and, as in 'gin with tonic'
came means arrived

explanation.surface: A son came along after work and departed in a vintage aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sopwith Camel was a British biplane fighter of the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: A First World War fighter aircraft, so an old plane.

clue.text: Successfully complete repair?

definitions.meaning: to settle something in one's favour, as in having the deal finished
literally, to mend with needle and thread; the question mark flags the literal reading

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to secure a deal and also, literally, to close a tear by stitching.

clue.text: Grim realities for a Hebrew

indicators.note: grim suggests something twisted and harsh, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Harsh truths endured by a Jewish person.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the ancient people of Israel, a Hebrew.

clue.text: Spooner's fault opening package for Christmas?

indicators.note: the clergyman Spooner swapped the starts of words, so the opening sounds of the two pieces trade places

parts.note: a rift is a fault, as in geology
a gap is an opening

explanation.surface: A defect in the opening of a festive parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: The swap works by sound: the result is heard as 'gift wrap', with the W silent. The question mark flags Christmas as just one occasion for wrapping presents.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap presents decoratively is to package them, as one does before Christmas.

clue.text: Band: T Rex up wearing outrageous gear

indicators.note: wearing means the reversed letters are dressed in the jumbled clothing
outrageous suggests wild disorder, so the letters of gear are jumbled
up in a down clue means the following letters are read upward, backwards

parts.note: Rex, Latin for king, is abbreviated R

explanation.surface: The glam rock group T. Rex climbing on stage in flamboyant costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outrageous' makes GAER from GEAR; 'up' turns T R into RT; 'wearing' puts RT inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of elastic worn round the leg to hold up a stocking is a band.

clue.text: Perhaps half of Republicans originally in dissenting group

indicators.note: in means that letter is placed inside the group

parts.note: a faction is a dissenting group within a party

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Maybe half the Republicans started out in a breakaway group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals that half is one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: One half is an example of a part of a whole number, so a fraction.

clue.text: Floats gently in water, at first, behind front of ship

indicators.note: in places the word for behind between the two picked letters
at first, echoed by front of, takes only the opening letter of water and of ship

parts.note: aft means behind, towards the stern

explanation.surface: Something drifts in the water, first behind the bow of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes W from water and 'front of' takes S from ship; AFT sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To drift lightly through air or water is to float gently.

clue.text: One practising self-denial in a British town? Almost right

indicators.note: almost means the town's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Staines is a town in Surrey, west of London

explanation.surface: An ascetic living in a British town, nearly upright.
explanation.walkthrough: STAINES is a commuter town on the Thames near Heathrow; 'Almost' drops its last S.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who refrains, especially from alcohol, practises self-denial.

clue.text: This sort of business meeting might end quickly

definitions.text: This sort of business meeting might end quickly

parts.words: This sort of business meeting might end quickly
parts.note: the second word read as two, break fast, is what ends a fast, and 'quickly' plays on fast

explanation.surface: A brisk work meeting might wrap up in no time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End quickly' reads as finishing in a hurry, but it means ending a period without food, which every morning meal does.
explanation.definitionFit: An early-morning working meal among executives is called by this name; the cryptic part is the meal ending a fast.

clue.text: Point at analyst producing computer program

parts.note: spell in the sense of signify or point to, as in 'that spells trouble'
a checker examines and analyses work

explanation.surface: Gesturing at an analyst who produces software.
explanation.walkthrough: SPELL for 'Point at' is loose; the nearest sense is signify, as in 'spells trouble'.
explanation.definitionFit: Software that flags misspelt words in a document is this kind of program.

clue.text: Carry out appliance

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to put a plan into effect
as a noun, a tool or device

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb meaning to put into effect and a noun meaning a tool or utensil.

clue.text: Small instrument for piercing

parts.note: a harp is a stringed musical instrument

explanation.surface: A little tool for making holes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' suggests a tool like an awl, but it is a musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with a fine point or keen edge is suited to piercing.

clue.text: Moan about having to guard silver dish

indicators.note: to guard means one piece surrounds and protects the other
about means the word for moan is turned round

parts.note: to sigh is to moan or lament
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about having to keep watch over the silverware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the word for moan, giving HGIS, and 'to guard' places silver's symbol within it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish pudding of offal, oatmeal and spices cooked in a casing is a traditional dish.

clue.text: "Material Girl"?

definitions.meaning: a thin silk or crepe dress fabric

explanation.walkthrough: The quotes evoke Madonna's song 'Material Girl', but the two words are separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a sheer crepe fabric and is also a woman's given name.

clue.text: Out? A Liberal admitting nothing speculative

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so the zero goes inside

parts.note: out means not in
O, the figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A Liberal, voted out and conceding nothing, is merely theorising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' puts O inside NOT IN, giving NOTION, before A and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Something existing only as an idea, hypothetical rather than real, is speculative.

clue.text: I harshly criticise a poor place in Pakistan

parts.note: to slam is to criticise harshly
bad means poor in quality

explanation.surface: Someone launches an attack on a deprived region of Pakistan.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Pakistan is a place in that country.

clue.text: A good many coming in to stock a number of small ships

indicators.note: coming in to means the word for many goes inside the word for stock

parts.note: to fill is to stock, as with shelves
a lot means a good many

explanation.surface: Plenty arriving to supply a fleet of little boats.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital A of the clue belongs to 'A good many'; the lower-case a at the end supplies the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fleet, a group of small vessels, is a flotilla.

clue.text: Especially a black protective coat Romeo discarded

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: discarded means the letter for Romeo is thrown away

parts.note: an overall is a coat worn to protect clothes
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Especially a black protective coat once Romeo has thrown it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discarded' takes R out of OVERALL, leaving OVEALL.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means more than anything else, in particular, which is what especially means.

clue.text: Minister in vicious circle

indicators.note: vicious suggests something wild and savage, so the letters of circle are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A government minister trapped in a self-perpetuating cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vicious circle' reads as a fixed phrase, but 'vicious' is the anagram signal; 'Minister' is a minister of religion.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman or priest is a minister of the church.

clue.text: Example that's missing in policy

indicators.note: that's missing means the following little word is removed

parts.note: an instance is an example

explanation.surface: A case that is absent from official policy.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is an attitude or position taken, a policy.

clue.text: Avid listener for example back inside

indicators.note: inside means the turned letters go within the organ of hearing

parts.note: an ear is what listens

indicators.note: back means the letters for for example are turned round

explanation.surface: A keen audience member, for example, sits at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'listener' is a crossword staple for the organ of hearing rather than a person; 'back' reverses the abbreviation, giving GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen, enthusiastic and impatient for something are near synonyms of avid.

clue.text: Odd drop of brandy before a dance

parts.note: rum is an old British word for odd or strange

indicators.note: drop of takes just the first little bit of brandy

explanation.surface: A curious nip of brandy before taking to the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' looks like an instruction to take odd letters, but it is RUM, meaning strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban ballroom dance is one example of a dance.

clue.text: Love entering closed place of worship on which there's a tribal emblem

definitions.text: on which there's a tribal emblem

parts.note: a door that is to is shut, so to means closed

indicators.note: entering means the zero goes inside the building

parts.note: a temple is a place of worship
love is zero in tennis, shown as O

explanation.surface: Love comes into a locked shrine marked with a tribal symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: TO for closed, as in 'pull the door to', is a crossword favourite; 'entering' puts O into TEMPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved post bearing the emblems of a clan or tribe, as made by Pacific Northwest peoples, is this.

clue.text: Bracing air round region

parts.note: O is round in shape
a zone is a region

explanation.surface: Refreshing breezes blowing around the area.
explanation.definitionFit: In everyday British usage, fresh invigorating seaside air is called this.

clue.text: Tripping over stand in the way, an obstacle

parts.note: stumbling means tripping over
to block is to stand in the way

explanation.surface: Falling over something blocking your route, a real hindrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A hindrance or difficulty that prevents progress is called this, an impediment.

clue.text: Individual copies turned over with speed

indicators.note: turned over means the word for copies is read backwards

parts.note: apes means copies, imitates
rate is speed, as in rate of knots

explanation.surface: Single copies are flipped over quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' makes SEPA from APES.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinct and apart from others, individual and separate are synonyms as adjectives.

clue.text: Miserable old doctor by organ

parts.note: the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: An unhappy elderly doctor working alongside an organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old' marks the word as archaic or poetic, part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary, dated form meaning dismal, gloomy and dull.
